title: Fixed-operator boundary extension audit for moving density interfaces
summary: Latushkin-Sukhtaiev expansions require a common symmetric operator and norm-C2 boundary path. The natural fixed-block pullback changes the principal coefficient, leaving a real applicability bridge open.
conditions: One fixed Hilbert space and densely defined closed symmetric A with equal deficiency indices
Fixed graph-norm bounded surjective trace satisfying the Green identity
Self-adjoint extensions T^{-1}(ran Q_t), with norm second-order expansion of Lagrangian orthogonal projections
Isolated finite-multiplicity spectral cluster; extra Z or Robin hypotheses when those formulas are used
scope: A source-to-project applicability diagnostic. It is not an eigenvalue or Hessian sign theorem for the moving-density problem.

content.missing_bridge: The expression differs on compactly supported interior tests; smooth matching equations alone do not make it an extension path of a common A. The bounded-additive Remark 2.14 does not cover a varying principal coefficient.
content.allowed_use: Organize trace, projection, normalization and path-acceleration obligations; use the separate bounded transfer proof for present P3.
content.prohibited_inference: No automatic substitution of density delta/delta-prime derivatives into L10; no global sign, G1 prime or uniqueness claim.

sources.locator: Project mapping and an explicit obstruction
sources.authorship: original author derivation or source adaptation, not independently accepted
